messages:
andrea: Heads-up — saw a regression on the multi-GPU TP pipeline after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. 1-step p99 latency up ~18% when KV cache is warm.
liam: ugh. Is that across all batch sizes or particular ones?
andrea: Mostly small batches (batch=1..4). Large batches are fine. Hypothesis: selector now prefers a different SGEMM/MatMul kernel for small sequence lengths.
sophia: do we have traces? nsys or timeline capture would be ideal.
andrea: here's the quick repro and a short nsys summary. Captured with: `nsys profile -o /tmp/post-probe --trace=cuda,nvtx python -m bench.run --model=tp4 --seq=32 --batch=2 --steps=50`
```
== PROCESSES: 1
Total CUDA API: 90 ms
GPU activities: 1120 ms
Kernel time breakdown:
  matmul_small_kernel : 520 ms
  matmul_large_kernel : 280 ms
  allreduce_kernel    : 180 ms
  kv_prefetch         : 40 ms
```
andrea: matmul_small_kernel used to be ~320ms previously. So ~200ms regression, not all from comm.
liam: interesting — allreduce doesn't look larger, so overlap failing. Is CUDA graph replay involved on the warm path?
andrea: yes. We replay graph on warm steps. The graph now captures the matmul on the default stream and the allreduce on a comm stream, but they don't overlap — seems like stream semantics changed during composer refactor.
raj: Can you paste the small snippet where kernels are launched / streams assigned?
andrea: snippet below — simplified:
```
// previous
cudaStream_t comp = default_stream();
cudaStream_t comm = create_stream_with_priority(low);
launch_matmul(comp,...);
enqueue_allreduce(comm,...);
// replay uses: capture(comp) then capture(comm)
```
Now after refactor the capture sequence is reordered by the new graph builder: comp capture gets implicitly serialized with comm due to a host-side sync introduced in `graph_builder::finalize()` (line ~432).
sophia: that host-sync was added to ensure deterministic submission ordering for mixed priority streams. But it could serialize if the graph uses external streams.
liam: can we test toggling that finalize path to avoid the host-side fence? maybe use `ALLOW_EXTERNAL_STREAM_ALIAS=1` env to reproduce without the fence.
andrea: tried that locally — when I skip the fence overlap returns and matmul drops back to ~340ms. So fence is likely culprit.
raj: what's the kernel selector change? any change log?
andrea: commit 9f8a2b8 adjusted `small_seq_threshold` from 48->32 to prefer `matmul_small_kernel` for lower memory footprint. That path combined with the fence makes the small kernel become the critical path.
liam: tl;dr: two orthogonal changes (kernel threshold + graph finalize fence) combined to kill overlap.
sophia: action items: 1) revert finalize fence for external-stream graphs OR add logic to keep comp/comm separate during capture 2) add perf regression test targeting warm-KV + graph replay + small batches 3) revert kernel threshold or make fallback to large kernel if overlap cost > X.
andrea: I'll open two PRs: one to gate the host-fence behind an env + unit test, one to add a canary perf job in CI that runs the repro and asserts p99 < baseline + 10%.
liam: also add a profiler check in the optimizer that flags when a selected kernel increases wall time vs an alternate because it kills overlap. We have historical cases where a smaller-memory kernel increases serialized execution.
raj: +1. For the canary please include nvtx markers and a micro-benchmark harness; latency variance is noisy.
andrea: noted. I'll also dump a full `nsys` timeline to shared/trace/2119999999.nsys and link from PR.
infra-bot: deploy-notes: staging will pick up PR #4821 once green; canary job template: perf/canary/kvcache-warm-graph.
liam: thanks. If we need a hotfix, revert the kernel-selector commit first since that has the least risk.
andrea: opening PRs now. Will post links when ready. :thumbsup:
